issue: Six pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3. Each stem either asks for a rule outright or restates a definition, so the skill is remembering, two levels below the label. The bank already labels its equivalent items remembering/1 or application/2, so the inflated labels skew the skill mix the readiness and Blueprint targets depend on.
evidence: fv-17 'For which item does HBU apply?' (recall: nonfinancial assets only). fv-25 'How are transaction costs treated?' (recall of the lesson takeaway). fv-28 'How is the fair value of a liability measured?', the same as fv-07, which is labeled remembering/1. fv-21 'quoted prices for similar bonds in active markets: what level?' restates the Level 2 definition, the same as x3-09 and x3-19 (remembering/1) and fv-01 (application/2). fv-26 'entity's own projections, no market data' restates the Level 3 definition, the same as fv-16 (application/2). fv-27 'L1, L2 and one significant L3 input', the same as fv-04 (application/2). None of the six has multiple steps, interrelationships or data to analyze.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions (Remembering & Understanding vs. Analysis); FAR skill allocation R&U 5-15%, Application 45-55%, Analysis 35-45% (content/sections/far.yaml)
fix: Relabel fv-17, fv-21, fv-25 and fv-28 to skill 'remembering', difficulty 1. Relabel fv-26 and fv-27 to 'application', difficulty 1-2, matching fv-16 and fv-04. Alternatively, rewrite them as real analysis items (e.g., give three inputs, ask which is significant and how that changes the level).

issue: Skill and/or difficulty labels are one level too high, and they are inconsistent with structurally identical items in the same bank.
evidence: fv-19 (50 - 3 transport = 47) and fv-23 (principal market price less transport) are analysis/3; fv-12 and chk1 are the identical task, labeled application/2. fv-24 (HBU, land worth more as residential) is analysis/3; fv-03 is the same scenario, labeled application/2. fv-09 (a forced sale is not orderly) is analysis/3 but is a one-step application of the 'orderly' definition. fv-15 (own credit goes to OCI) is application/3 but is pure recall (chk2, which also requires the split computation, is application). fv-18 (define fair value) is application/2 but is pure recall, like pre1 (remembering). fv-13 is difficulty 3 but needs no arithmetic: read the principal-market price.
fix: fv-19 and fv-23: application, difficulty 2. fv-24: application, difficulty 2. fv-09: application, difficulty 1-2. fv-15: remembering, difficulty 1. fv-18: remembering, difficulty 1. fv-13: difficulty 2.

issue: calc:true is set on items that need no computation.
evidence: fv-11: the stem states that a market participant would pay $92,000 and the key is $92,000; there is nothing to compute. fv-13: the key is the stated principal-market price of $40 with no transport cost, so no arithmetic is needed (only the distractors involve subtraction).
source: src/content/schema.ts (calc flag: items that need a computation)
fix: Set calc:false on fv-11 and fv-13 (or, for fv-13, add a transport cost so the key requires a subtraction).

issue: The answer is given away: the stem says a market participant 'would pay $92,000 for it today in an orderly transaction', which is the definition of fair value with the number filled in. The item tests nothing beyond reading the stem.
evidence: Stem: 'A market participant would pay $92,000 for it today in an orderly transaction.' Key (d): '$92,000'. The (a) trap is also mislabeled 'wrong-classification' for the entry-price error, which pre1(a) and fv-18(a) label 'reversed'.
source: ASC 820-10-35-2 (fair value is a market-based exit price)
fix: Make the learner choose among data: e.g., cost $100,000; entity's value in use $105,000; dealer bid in an orderly sale $92,000; liquidation bid $80,000. Ask for fair value. Relabel the (a) trap 'reversed'.

issue: The item does not discriminate the principal-market rule from the most-advantageous-market rule: the principal market also gives the better net amount, so a learner who wrongly applies 'most advantageous' still reaches the key. The explanation's claim 'even if another market offers a better net price' does not describe this item's facts.
evidence: Principal market net = 40 - 4 = 36; other market net = 42 - 7 = 35. The principal market wins under both rules, and only a learner who picks the highest gross price ($42) misses.
fix: Change the other market's transaction costs to $1 (net 41 > 36), so 'most advantageous' points to the other market and only the principal-market rule gives $40. Add distractor $41 (other market's net) and keep $42.

issue: In Market B the transaction costs equal the transport costs ($2 each), so a learner who makes the reversed error (deducting transaction costs instead of transport) still reaches the key of $96. The item cannot detect the core misconception it is meant to test. Distractor (a) $94 is also produced by Market A's price less transaction costs.
evidence: B: 98 - 2 transport = 96 (key); 98 - 2 transaction = 96 (reversed error, same number). A: 100 - 6 = 94 = option (a); 100 - 2 = 98 = option (c); 100 - 6 - 2 = 92 = option (d).
fix: Change Market B's transaction costs to $1 (net 95 vs. A's 92, so B is still most advantageous; FV 96; the reversed error then gives 97, which can be a distractor). Update fv-23, which reuses these numbers, so both stay consistent.

issue: Some distractor rationales and trap labels do not describe the error that actually produces the option.
evidence: fv-12 (d) $47 = 50 - 3 transaction (the reversed swap of transaction and transport), but its explanation 'Transaction costs aren't deducted' is identical to (b)'s, it omits that transport was not deducted, and it is trapped 'wrong-rule'; the same error is 'reversed' in chk1(c) and fv-19(d). fv-22 (d) $92 = A's 100 - 6 - 2 (wrong market AND transaction costs deducted); the explanation says only 'B is most advantageous'. fv-22 (c) $98 is also A's 100 - 2 (wrong market), not only B's undeducted price. chk2 (a) and fv-15 (a), own credit in net income, model the pre-ASU 2016-01 rule but are trapped 'partial-computation' and 'wrong-classification'; the schema offers 'outdated-rule'. fv-11 (a), entry price: 'wrong-classification' vs. 'reversed' (see the fv-11 finding).
fix: fv-12 (d): 'This deducts the $3 transaction costs instead of the $2 transport costs', trap 'reversed'. fv-22 (d): 'Uses Market A and deducts transaction costs; B nets more (94 vs. 92) and FV deducts only transport.' fv-22 (c): mention both routes to 98. chk2 (a) and fv-15 (a): trap 'outdated-rule', noting it was the pre-ASU 2016-01 treatment.

issue: calc items' overall explanations state the rule but show no computation, contrary to the schema's 'full computation when calculation-based'. Contrast fv-02, whose explanation shows the net amounts and the result.
evidence: chk2: no 400,000 - 150,000 = 250,000, and no note that a decrease in a liability is a gain. fv-12: no 50 - 2 = 48. fv-13: no numbers. fv-19: no 50 - 3 = 47. fv-22: no nets (A 92, B 94) and no 98 - 2 = 96. fv-23: no 100 - 2 = 98.
fix: Add the computation to each, e.g., fv-22: 'Net: A = 100 - 6 - 2 = 92; B = 98 - 2 - 2 = 94 -> B. FV = 98 - 2 = **96**.'

issue: Distractor explanations are circular or too terse to teach, and one is confusing.
evidence: fv-24 (c) and fv-25 (d): 'That is not the rule.' fv-25 (b) 'They are not deducted.' and (c) 'They are not added.' fv-26 (d) 'It is permitted.' fv-21 (d) 'It is a fair value measure.' fv-16 (d) 'Level 3 inputs are allowed.' fv-15 (b) 'The change is recognized.' fv-28 (b) 'Not fair value.' fv-08 (d) 'Implicit for all.' fv-27 (a) 'Not the highest level.' is confusing because Level 1 IS the highest level of the hierarchy; the point is that categorization follows the lowest significant input.
fix: State the rule and why the option fails, e.g., fv-24 (c): 'Fair value isn't a lower-of comparison; it is the value under the market participants' highest and best use.' fv-27 (a): 'Categorization follows the lowest-level significant input (Level 3), not the highest-level input used.' fv-25 (b): 'Transaction costs are specific to the transaction, not the asset (820-10-35-9B); they are used only to choose the most advantageous market.'

issue: Throwaway fourth distractors that no prepared candidate would pick, which makes these effectively 3-option items.
evidence: fv-16 (d) 'It can't be measured'; fv-20 (d) 'The equity method' (not a valuation approach); fv-21 (d) 'Not a fair value measure'; fv-26 (d) 'Not permitted'; fv-25 (d) 'They're deducted only for Level 3'.
fix: Replace them with plausible misconceptions, e.g., fv-16/fv-26: 'Level 2, because a discount rate is used'; fv-21: 'Level 1, because the market is active'; fv-20: 'Market approach, because royalty rates are observable'; fv-25: 'Deducted, because the most advantageous market is chosen on a net basis'.

issue: The same fact ('quoted prices for similar assets in active markets = Level 2') is tested the same way four times. Two of the four are near-clone exam-pool items used across the mocks, and the practice item fv-01 is a near-verbatim copy of the mock item x3-09, so the mocks test recall of a practiced item.
evidence: cues.md: fv-01 ~ x3-09 Jaccard 0.86. x3-19 is a reworded x3-09 (same four option types). Mock usage: x3-09 appears in far-mock-1 AND far-mock-3; x3-19 in far-mock-2. The same fact also appears in lesson faded step 2 and TBS row l4.
fix: Rewrite x3-19 to test a different Level 2 input (a quoted price in an inactive market, or a swap valued with observable SOFR curves) or a Level 2 vs. Level 3 judgment (an observable input adjusted by a significant unobservable input). Rewrite fv-21 as a multi-input scenario. Avoid using x3-09 in two mock forms.

issue: The same computation ('principal-market price less transport, transaction costs ignored') is tested the same way four times with nearly identical numbers, plus fv-25 (recall of the same rule) and TBS row pp.
evidence: chk1 $50/tc 4/transport 3 -> 47; fv-12 $50/tc 3/transport 2 -> 48; fv-19 $50/transport 3/tc 2 -> 47 (cues.md: fv-12 ~ fv-19 Jaccard 0.80, swapped numbers); fv-23 $100/tc 6/transport 2 -> 98.
fix: Keep chk1 and fv-23. Repurpose fv-12 or fv-19 to an untested concept, e.g., a financial asset where location is not a characteristic (no transport deduction), or bid-ask pricing (ASC 820-10-35-36C).

issue: The later half of the practice bank largely re-asks earlier items one-for-one in thinner form, so 28 practice MCQs cover only about 14 distinct facts.
evidence: Near-clone pairs: fv-04/fv-27 (lowest significant input); fv-07/fv-28 (liability = transfer price, nonperformance risk); fv-16/fv-26 (own projections = Level 3); fv-03/fv-24 (HBU land; x3-28 makes 3); fv-10/fv-14 (P x Q, no blockage; fv-14's stem even says 'Level 1 fair value', which cues the unadjusted price); chk2/fv-15 (own credit to OCI; far-bond-28 in far-bonds is a third near-verbatim copy).
fix: Replace the second item of each pair with an untested concept: transaction price vs. fair value at initial recognition (820-10-30-3); premiums and discounts vs. unit of account (820-10-35-36B); contractual sale restrictions (ASU 2022-03); the current use presumed to be HBU (820-10-35-10E); the bid-ask spread; a liability's fair value with nonperformance risk computed; FVO eligibility (PP&E vs. an equity-method investment).

issue: The stem is garbled: 'Which Level 3 disclosure is required but not required for Level 1 recurring measurements?' contradicts itself on a first read.
evidence: Stem as written. Intended: a disclosure required for recurring Level 3 measurements but not for recurring Level 1 measurements.
fix: Reword: 'For recurring fair value measurements, which disclosure is required for Level 3 measurements but not for Level 1 measurements of a public business entity?'

issue: The lesson and fv-08 present the Level 3 reconciliation (roll-forward) as required for all entities. Since ASU 2018-13, nonpublic entities instead disclose purchases and issues of Level 3 items and transfers into and out of Level 3.
evidence: Lesson: 'Level 3 measurements require the most disclosure, including a reconciliation of beginning and ending balances...' fv-08 key explanation: 'Level 3 recurring measurements require a roll-forward (reconciliation)...' Neither mentions the entity type.
source: ASC 820-10-50-2(c) and 820-10-50-2F (ASU 2018-13, effective FY beginning after 12/15/2019)
fix: Add to the lesson: 'Public business entities present a Level 3 roll-forward; nonpublic entities may instead disclose Level 3 purchases, issues and transfers in or out.' Specify 'public business entity' in the fv-08 stem.

issue: Lesson-item alignment: items and the TBS test three rules the lesson never teaches.
evidence: (1) Level 1 = quoted price x quantity, and blockage factors are prohibited: fv-10, fv-14. The lesson never mentions P x Q or blockage. (2) A liability's fair value is a transfer price (not settlement with the creditor) and includes nonperformance risk: fv-07, fv-28. The lesson only says 'paid to transfer a liability'. (3) The entity's normal market is presumed to be the principal market, judged from the entity's perspective: the TBS exhibit gives 'Share of Prairie's historical volume' and the pp explanation says only 'greatest volume'. The lesson's 'greatest volume and activity' doesn't tell a learner that the entity's own volume share is the relevant evidence. The TBS research part and fv-13 also rely on the 35-6 rule that the principal market is used 'even if' another market is more advantageous, which the lesson implies but never states.
fix: Add to 'Which market, and which costs?': 'If a principal market exists, use it even if another market nets more (35-6); the market the entity normally uses is presumed to be the principal market.' Add a short 'Liabilities' paragraph (transfer, not settlement; includes nonperformance risk, including own credit) and a Level 1 bullet: 'P x Q; no blockage discount, at any level.'

issue: The explanations say blockage factors are prohibited 'for Level 1', which implies they may be allowed at Levels 2 and 3. ASC 820 prohibits blockage factors at every level; only premiums or discounts that are a characteristic of the asset (consistent with its unit of account) are allowed in Level 2/3 measurements.
evidence: fv-10 (c): 'ASC 820 prohibits blockage factors for Level 1 measurements.' fv-14 (a): 'Blockage discounts aren't allowed for Level 1.' fv-14 (b): 'No premium applies to a Level 1 measurement.'
fix: Reword to: 'A blockage factor (a discount for the size of the entity's holding) is never permitted in a fair value measurement; for a Level 1 asset, fair value is P x Q.'

issue: The stem omits the highest-and-best-use conditions (physically possible, legally permissible, financially feasible), so whether the residential use is available (e.g., zoning) is left unstated. fv-03, the near-duplicate, states them.
evidence: Stem: 'Land used as a factory site would be worth more to market participants as residential land.' Nothing says rezoning is permitted or probable.
fix: Add 'Residential use is legally permitted and financially feasible', or retire fv-24 as a duplicate of fv-03 (see the redundancy finding).

issue: Several ASC paragraph references point to the adjacent paragraph rather than the one that states the rule, and the TBS research key is not the best available citation.
evidence: fv-12 cites 820-10-35-9B for the transport adjustment; 35-9B covers transaction costs and 35-9C covers transport costs (location as a characteristic). TBS research excerpt [b] attributes both to 35-9B. fv-13 cites 35-5 for 'even if another market offers a better net price'; that is 35-6. TBS research: the prompt asks why Chicago is used 'even though the local elevator would net more', which 35-6 answers directly; the keyed excerpt [a] (35-5) states only the general principal/most-advantageous rule. Distractor [d] cites 825-10-25-4 (election dates) for 'instrument-by-instrument and irrevocable', which is 825-10-25-2.
fix: fv-12: cite 820-10-35-9B and 35-9C. fv-13: cite 820-10-35-6. TBS: change excerpt [a] to 'ASC 820-10-35-6: if there is a principal market, fair value is the price in that market even if the price in a different market is potentially more advantageous'; cite [b] as 35-9B/9C; cite [d] as 825-10-25-2.

issue: Coverage gaps: the lesson and items omit ASC 820 points that are currently testable and exam-relevant. The most notable is ASU 2022-03 (contractual sale restrictions on equity securities are not considered in fair value and are disclosed), effective for PBEs in fiscal years beginning after 12/15/2023 and so testable since 2024. Also missing: the transaction price vs. fair value at initial recognition, and the presumption that an asset's current use is its HBU.
evidence: No item, flashcard or lesson text mentions sale restrictions, ASU 2022-03, 820-10-30-3 (entry price = exit price at initial recognition, with exceptions), or 820-10-35-10E. review/reference/far-standards.md lists ASU 2022-03 (PBE FY > 12/15/2023). ASU 2026-03 (investment-company exception) is correctly absent (eligible 2028).
fix: Add a sentence and one MCQ on ASU 2022-03 (a lock-up on a listed share is not a characteristic of the security -> Level 1 P x Q, no discount; disclose the restriction). Add a line on the transaction price vs. fair value at initial recognition. Use the redundant slots identified elsewhere.

issue: Possible 2026 Blueprint scope mismatch. The 2026 FAR Blueprint removed two fair-value representative tasks and added one to re-align ASC 820 between FAR and BAR. The repo's reference notes say FAR 'now appears limited to concepts and the hierarchy, with measurement calculations in BAR'. If so, the lesson objective 'Determine the fair value of an asset or liability' (application), the TBS wheat computation and about nine calc MCQs (chk1, fv-02, fv-10, fv-12, fv-13, fv-14, fv-19, fv-22, fv-23) may exceed FAR scope and should be marked optional or kept only as concept checks. The exact task text was not confirmed.
evidence: review/reference/blueprint-notes.md FAR 2026 change 4 ('exact new task text was not seen'); review/reference/far-standards.md §1b marks the count as 'conflict'. Two web searches (UWorld, Becker summaries) confirmed a FAR/BAR ASC 820 realignment but disagreed on the task count (one vs. two removed) and did not give the task text.
source: AICPA Summary of Changes to the Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints effective 1/1/2026 (via https://accounting.uworld.com/cpa-review/cpa-exam/changes and https://www.becker.com/blog/cpa/new-cpa-exam-exposure-draft search results)
fix: Have an expert read the 2026 FAR Blueprint Area III.E task text. If measurement calculations moved to BAR, tag the lesson objective task accordingly and either mark the calc items and the TBS 'wheat' part optional or reframe them as concept items (principal vs. most advantageous, cost treatment) without heavy arithmetic.

issue: In the worked example both scenarios land on Market A, so the lesson never shows the case that the TBS research part and fv-13/fv-23 test: a principal market that nets less than another market but still governs.
evidence: Worked example: Market A principal -> 28; no principal: A nets 25 vs. B 24 -> A -> 28. The contrast case (principal market nets less) never appears.
fix: Change Market B to price $35, transaction $6, transport $2 (net 27 > A's 25). Then 'A principal -> FV 28 even though B nets more' and 'no principal -> B most advantageous -> FV 33'.

issue: The flashcard drops the condition on the transport-cost rule: transport costs are deducted only if location is a characteristic of the asset (e.g., a commodity). The lesson states it correctly.
evidence: Back: 'Transport costs: deducted.'
fix: Back: 'Transaction costs: not deducted (only used to pick the most advantageous market). Transport costs: deducted when location is a characteristic of the asset.'
